intro: Match each piece of evidence to what it means. That's the "so what."

left.label: Locke: when a legislature grabs absolute power, the power passes back to the people.
hints: What happens to a government that abuses its power?
Look for the choice about keeping power only while protecting rights.

left.label: Montesquieu: there is no liberty when one person both makes and enforces the laws.
hints: Montesquieu's answer was to divide power.

left.label: Rousseau: the general will looks only at the common interest.
hints: The general will isn't just counting votes.
Look for the choice about a majority.

left.label: Wollstonecraft: prove first that women lack reason, or stop shutting them out.
hints: Wollstonecraft used the philosophes' own idea against them.

left.label: Catherine's government punishes serfs who complain about their landlords.
hints: Catherine wrote about equal laws. Did serfs get them?
Look for the choice about her promise.

left.label: Hobbes: without a power over everyone, people live in a state of war.
hints: Hobbes thought life without government was war. So what would people do?

right.label: …which means a government only keeps its power as long as it protects people's rights.
…which means the only safe government is one where power is split and each part checks the others.
…which means a majority isn't automatically right if it only adds up what each person wants.
…which means the Enlightenment's own rule, that rights come from reason, should include women.
…which means her promise of equal laws never reached the people at the bottom.
…which means people will accept a strong ruler just to escape the fear.

rationale.a: If power passes back to the people when a government abuses it, then a government only keeps power while it protects their rights.
rationale.b: If united power destroys liberty, the fix is to split it so each part checks the others.
rationale.c: If the general will is about the common interest, then adding up private wants, even a majority's, can still get it wrong.
rationale.d: The philosophes said rights come from reason. Wollstonecraft's dare means that if women can reason, their rights follow.
rationale.e: Punishing serfs for complaining means the equal laws Catherine wrote about never reached them.
rationale.f: If life without government is war, people will trade freedom for safety and accept a strong ruler.
